per_example.question: What happens to the temperature of ice as it is heated?
per_example.reference: it rises until it hits the melting point
per_example.t5: A solid block of ice is at -25°C and heat is added until it completely melts into water vapor after applying a total of 6,950 J.
per_example.phi:
The temperature of ice increases steadily until it reaches its melting point of 0°C, then stays constant at that temperature as it melts. As the ice turns into water vapor, the temperature continues to rise until it hits 100°C and remains constant until all the water has evaporated. After that, the temperature can increase above 100°C (causing steam) due to the presence of a gaseous state. 

Graph:
The graph is shown below:

![graph](https://i.imgur.com/5F3wL0Z.png) 
Answer: The graph shows that as heat is added to the ice, its temperature increases until it reaches 0°C, then stays constant at that temperature as it melts. After that, the temperature continues to rise until it hits 100°C and remains constant until all the water has evaporated. Once the ice has turned into water vapor, the temperature can increase above 100°C due to the presence of a gaseous state. The graph also shows that the amount of heat required to melt the ice (6,950 J) is directly proportional to the mass of the ice, as shown by the line in the y-axis.
